concept: Why does ice float on water?
title: Frozen Harbor
tagline: Heavy ice that refuses to sink

science.hiddenLaw: Archimedes' principle: F_buoyant = rho_fluid * V_displaced * g, equal to the weight of displaced fluid. At equilibrium floating, F_buoyant = W_object, so V_submerged/V_total = rho_object/rho_fluid, and an object floats iff rho_object < rho_fluid. For H2O, rho_ice ≈ 917 kg/m³ < rho_water ≈ 1000 kg/m³ at 0-4°C because hydrogen bonding forms an open hexagonal crystal that occupies ~9% more volume than liquid water.
science.plainStatement: Ice floats because the same weight of ice takes up more space than liquid water — it is less dense — so the water it pushes aside weighs enough to hold it up.
misconceptions: Floating/sinking depends on absolute weight or mass (heavier things sink, lighter things float) rather than density relative to the fluid.
Ice floats because of trapped air bubbles, cold temperature, or surface tension, not because its crystal structure makes it intrinsically less dense than liquid water.
Colder always means denser, so ice must be denser than liquid water and should sink.

story.setting: A quiet harbor in winter. A single clear block bobs at the waterline.
story.mystery: Why does solid ice sit high instead of sinking like a stone?
story.goal: Adjust the block and water to discover what decides floating.

predictions.prompt: You make the block ten times bigger but keep its density the same. What happens?
options: It floats with same share below
It rises higher out of water

predictions.prompt: Clear bubble-free ice still floats. Why?
options: Crystal structure makes it less dense

predictions.prompt: Water freezes into ice. What happens to its density?
options: It gets denser and should sink
It gets less dense and floats

transfer.setup: A research balloon cabin on a distant moon must float in a cold methane sea. The cabin averages 850 kg per cubic metre, the methane sea is 1020 kg per cubic metre.
transfer.question: How will the cabin sit in the methane sea?

checks.description: Ice density 917 in water 1000 floats with ~91.7% submerged, V_sub/V_total = rho_ice/rho_water
Control: remove cause - make fluid less dense than ice (800 kg/m3) -> ice no longer floats, it sinks
Buoyant force equals weight of displaced fluid at equilibrium
Misconception test: 10x larger mass but same density (917) still floats at same ~91.7% fraction, disproving absolute-weight theory
